title: Two-degree coherent structure model for a proper flat curve family
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper flat morphism of finite presentation of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For every $s\in S$ write $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-base-change, def-weil-residue-field]. Assume $\dim(X_s)\leq1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and that the structural map $\kappa(s)\to H^0(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})$ is bijective [pqf-def-cohomology]. Put $K=Rf_*(\mathcal O_X[0])$ [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-direct-image], and let $u:\mathcal O_S[0]\to K$ be the derived structural unit, whose map on degree-zero cohomology is the structural function pullback. Then $K$ is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex], $H^0(u):\mathcal O_S\to H^0(K)$ is invertible, and $E=H^1(K)$ is quasi-coherent and finite locally free [pqf-def-coherent, def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf]. Zariski-locally on $S$ there is an isomorphism
$$K\cong\mathcal O_S[0]\oplus E[-1],$$
where $E[-1]$ places $E$ in cohomological degree one. In particular $H^i(K)=0$ for $i\notin\{0,1\}$. For every morphism $g:T\to S$, put $X_T=X\times_ST$ and let $f_T:X_T\to T$ be the projection. The canonical derived module base-change map [def-pc-derived-module-base-change-map]
$$\delta_g:Lg^*K\longrightarrow Rf_{T,*}(\mathcal O_{X_T}[0])$$
is an isomorphism; no flatness of $g$, reducedness of $S$, or constancy of the local rank of $E$ on all of $S$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0GKA, label lemma-genus-in-nodal-family-of-curves, proof from the local decomposition through the finite-free residue model; the argument uses only proper flat finite presentation, fibrewise constant functions and fibre dimension at most one, rather than the nodal hypothesis.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-rf-perfect-base-change] to $\mathcal G=\mathcal O_X$. This module has the one-element presentation with no relations, and is flat over $S$ by the assumed flatness of $f$. Thus $K=Rf_*(\mathcal O_X[0])$ is perfect. Moreover, for every $g:T\to S$ its canonical module base-change map is invertible. The ordinary tensor pullback of $\mathcal O_X$ is $\mathcal O_{X_T}$: multiplication identifies $\mathcal O_{X_T}\otimes_{g_X^{-1}\mathcal O_X}g_X^{-1}\mathcal O_X$ with $\mathcal O_{X_T}$. Consequently the map in that lemma is precisely $\delta_g$ of the statement. Also [lem-sc-perfect-qcoherent] gives quasi-coherence of every $H^i(K)$, in particular of $E=H^1(K)$.

source.place: Tag 0B91, lemma-flat-proper-perfect-direct-image-general (2); its specialization in the proof of Tag 0GKA

proof.text: Properness makes $f$ quasi-compact and separated. Apply [lem-sc-flat-derived-structure-unit] to obtain a map $a:\mathcal O_S[0]\to K$ whose degree-zero map is the structural map and whose residue pullbacks have zero negative cohomology. At every $s$, the assumed bijection $\kappa(s)\to H^0(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})$ makes $H^0(Li_s^*a)$ invertible. Step 1 makes $K$ perfect with quasi-coherent cohomology. Therefore [lem-sc-perfect-degree-zero-fibre-criterion], applied to this $a$, shows that $H^0(a)$ is invertible and supplies an open cover on which $K\cong\mathcal O_S[0]\oplus P$, with $P$ perfect of Tor-amplitude in $[1,\infty)$. Under the canonical identification $H^0(K)=f_*\mathcal O_X$, both $H^0(a)$ and the stated $H^0(u)$ are the structural function pullback; hence $H^0(u)$ is invertible. Only equality of their degree-zero maps is needed.

source.place: Tag 0E62, lemma-proper-flat-h0, proof; the initial local decomposition in Tag 0GKA

proof.text: For every $s\in S$, properness includes finite type, so [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](2) makes $X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ finite type. A field has only the ideals $0$ and the whole field, and its spectrum is a single point, so $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $X_s$ is Noetherian. Its dimension is at most one by hypothesis. The structure sheaf is quasi-coherent (on an affine open it is the sheaf associated to the ring itself). Thus [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension] gives $H^i(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})=0$ for $i>1$. Step 1, with $g=i_s$, identifies $H^i(Li_s^*K)$ with these groups: direct image to the one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is global sections, and its right derived functor is sheaf cohomology.

source.place: Tag 0GKA, lemma-genus-in-nodal-family-of-curves, proof: residue cohomology and Proposition 02UZ

proof.text: Work on an open of the decomposition in step 2, and fix $s$ there. Since $P$ has Tor-amplitude in $[1,\infty)$, $H^i(Li_s^*P)=0$ for $i<1$. Pulling the direct sum of step 2 to $s$, its degree $i>1$ cohomology is $H^i(Li_s^*P)=H^i(Li_s^*K)=0$ by step 3, because the other summand is $\kappa(s)[0]$. Hence the only possibly nonzero residue Betti number of $P$ is $d_1$. Apply [lem-sc-perfect-finite-free-residue-model] on this open. After shrinking around $s$, its finite free representative has zero terms in every degree other than one and term $\mathcal O^{\oplus d_1}$ in degree one. Its differentials are therefore zero. Its cohomology is zero outside degree one, and $H^1(P)$ on this neighbourhood is $\mathcal O^{\oplus d_1}$. The decomposition identifies $H^1(P)$ with $E$. These neighbourhoods cover $S$, so $E$ is finite locally free, $P\cong E[-1]$ on each such neighbourhood, and $K\cong\mathcal O_S[0]\oplus E[-1]$ there. Computing cohomology of this explicit complex gives $H^i(K)=0$ locally, hence globally, for $i\notin\{0,1\}$.
